practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly provided?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 178 of the Indian Constitution requires every Legislative Assembly of a State to, as soon as may be, choose two members of the Assembly to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Article 182 relates to the Legislative Council Chairman and Deputy Chairman.

practiceQuestions.q: Who elects the Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly?
opts: All citizens of the State through direct election
The members of the Legislative Assembly from amongst themselves
The Chief Minister in consultation with the cabinet
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker is elected by the Legislative Assembly from amongst its own members. Once a vacancy occurs in the office of the Speaker, the Assembly chooses another member to fill the vacancy.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly submit their resignation?
opts: The Deputy Speaker of the Assembly
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly submits their resignation letter to the Deputy Speaker of the Assembly. Similarly, the Deputy Speaker submits their resignation to the Speaker.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the tenure of the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly?
opts: As long as they enjoy the pleasure of the Governor
Generally life of the Assembly, unless they cease to be a member earlier
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker remains in office during the life of the Assembly. However, they vacate office earlier if: (a) they cease to be a member of the assembly, (b) they resign, or (c) they are removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the assembly.

practiceQuestions.q: Who appoints the 'Pro-Tem Speaker' of a newly elected State Legislative Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Governor appoints a member of the Legislative Assembly as the Speaker Pro Tem. Usually, the senior most member of the House is chosen for this temporary post to preside over the first session of the new assembly and administer oaths to new members.

practiceQuestions.q: When does the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly vacate their office even after the dissolution of the Assembly?
opts: Immediately when the Governor orders dissolution
Immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Assembly
When the new Chief Minister takes oath
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike Lok Sabha where the Speaker vacates office immediately before the newly elected House meets, the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly does not vacate office on the dissolution of the Assembly and continues until immediately before the first meeting of the assembly after the dissolution.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the casting vote exercised by the Speaker used for?
opts: To pass a Money Bill in the first instance
To resolve a tie when votes are equally divided
To veto any bill passed by the assembly
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker does not vote in the first instance. They have a 'casting vote' which is used only in the case of a tie (when there is an equality of votes on a resolution or bill). The objective is to maintain the status quo or break a deadlock.

practiceQuestions.q: Who certifies whether a bill introduced in the State Legislative Assembly is a Money Bill or not?
opts: The Advocate General of the State
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly has the exclusive and final power to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill or not, and their decision in this regard cannot be questioned in any court.

practiceQuestions.q: Under which schedule of the Constitution does the Speaker decide questions of disqualification of MLAs on the ground of defection?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution (Anti-Defection Law), the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly is the authority to decide questions regarding the disqualification of a member of the House on grounds of defection.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the quorum to constitute a meeting of the State Legislative Assembly?
opts: One-third of the total members of the House
One-tenth of the total members of the House or 10 members, whichever is greater
One-half of the total members of the House
practiceQuestions.sol: The quorum to constitute a meeting of the Legislative Assembly is 10 members or one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, whichever is higher, as per Article 189(3).

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly not vacate office immediately upon dissolution of the House, unlike the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
opts: Because state assemblies have bicameral legislatures in all states.
To ensure continuity of administrative duties related to the upcoming transition and first meeting under constitutional convention and specific state provisions.
Because the Governor directly appoints the next Speaker before dissolution.
To enable the Speaker to act as Governor during the interregnum.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 179(b) explicitly provides that a Speaker vacates their office not upon dissolution, but immediately before the first meeting of the assembly after the dissolution. This is designed to keep the presiding office functional for any emergent administrative tasks and till the pro-tem speaker/new speaker selection takes place.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the position of the Deputy Speaker differ from that of the Speaker regarding subordination to the Speaker?
opts: The Deputy Speaker is subordinate to the Speaker in all legislative actions.
The Deputy Speaker is subordinate to the Speaker and takes orders directly from them.
The Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker; they are independently elected by the Assembly and answerable only to the House.
The Deputy Speaker can overrule the Speaker's rulings during assembly sessions.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker. They hold an independent office and are responsible directly to the House. When presiding over the House, they possess the same powers as the Speaker.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens when a resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration in the Legislative Assembly?
opts: The Speaker must immediately resign from the Assembly membership.
The Speaker cannot preside over the sitting of the House, but has the right to speak and take part in its proceedings and vote in the first instance.
The Speaker is barred from entering the assembly premises entirely.
The Speaker retains the right to preside over the sitting during the debate on the removal motion.
practiceQuestions.sol: When a resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration, the Speaker cannot preside, though they are present. However, unlike when they preside, they have the right to speak, take part in proceedings, and vote in the first instance (though not with a casting vote).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the principle of 'Impartiality of the Speaker' in the Indian parliamentary system?
opts: The Speaker must resign from their political party immediately upon election to the post.
The Speaker convention of not contesting elections again after tenure ends.
An institutional convention where the Speaker severs active political ties and remains neutral in conduct, although resignation from party membership is not legally mandated in India.
The Speaker is appointed by the opposition party to ensure checks and balances.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike the British system where the Speaker strictly resigns from political affiliations, in India, resignation from party membership is not constitutionally required. However, the convention is expected that the Speaker acts with absolute neutrality and impartiality in discharging official duties.

practiceQuestions.q: If both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly are absent, who presides over the meeting of the Assembly?
opts: A member determined by the rules of procedure of the House (Panel of Chairpersons)
The senior-most judge of the State High Court
practiceQuestions.sol: If both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are absent, any such member of the assembly as may be determined by the rules of procedure of the House (typically a member from a panel of chairpersons nominated by the Speaker) presides.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the Speaker's nomination of chairpersons to various committees of the Legislative Assembly?
opts: It ensures executive control over legislative scrutiny.
It underpins the Speaker's administrative control over the internal working and oversight mechanism of the legislature.
It transfers all budgetary powers to the Governor.
It allows the Chief Minister to draft laws directly.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker appoints chairpersons of all committees of the assembly, which empowers the presiding officer to shape legislative oversight, policy examination, and maintain effective parliamentary control over executive actions through specialized committees.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the decision of the Speaker regarding disqualification under the Tenth Schedule be subjected to judicial review?
opts: No, it is completely immune from judicial scrutiny under all circumstances.
Yes, as ruled in the landmark Kihoto Hollohan case, the Speaker's decision is subject to judicial review on grounds like mala fides, perversity, or violation of natural justice.
Yes, but only by the Supreme Court of India directly, bypassing High Courts.
No, because the Speaker acts as a judicial tribunal whose orders are final.
practiceQuestions.sol: In the landmark 'Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu' (1992) case, the Supreme Court held that the Tenth Schedule is constitutional, but the Speaker's decision while acting as a tribunal is subject to judicial review on limited grounds such as unconstitutionality, mala fides, perversity, and violation of natural justice.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of the financial autonomy of the Legislative Assembly, what role does the Speaker play?
opts: The Speaker prepares the state budget along with the Finance Minister.
The Speaker has control over the Secretariat of the Assembly, and the expenses of the Assembly are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The Speaker allocates funds for developmental schemes in MLAs' constituencies.
The Speaker audits the accounts of the state government.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker ensures the financial independence of the legislature. The Secretariat of the Assembly is independent, and administrative expenses of the assembly, including salaries of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, are 'charged' upon the Consolidated Fund of the State (not subject to vote).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of appointing a 'Pro-Tem Speaker' in a newly constituted Legislative Assembly?
opts: To conduct the election of the permanent Speaker and administer oaths to newly elected MLAs.
To pass the annual vote-on-account before the cabinet is formed.
To negotiate coalition government terms among political parties.
To frame the new legislative agenda for the next five years.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pro-Tem Speaker is a temporary officer appointed specifically to administer oaths to the newly elected members of the Legislative Assembly and to preside over the election of the regular Speaker.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article protects the proceedings of the Legislative Assembly from being questioned in any court regarding irregularity of procedure?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 212 of the Constitution provides that the validity of any proceedings in the Legislature of a State shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure, and no officer or member of the Legislature in whom powers are vested shall be subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of the exercise of those powers.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly:
1. The Speaker is elected by the Legislative Assembly from amongst its members soon after its first meeting.
2. Whenever the Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker vacates his office immediately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Speaker is chosen by the assembly from amongst its members under Article 178. Statement 2 is incorrect: Unlike the Lok Sabha Speaker, the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly does not vacate office upon dissolution of the assembly; they remain in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected assembly.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly:
1. The office of the Deputy Speaker is specifically created by Article 178 of the Indian Constitution.
2. When the office of the Speaker is vacant, the Deputy Speaker performs all the duties of the Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 178 provides for both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker. When the Speaker's office is vacant, the Deputy Speaker performs their duties and has the same powers when presiding over the house.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers and functions of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly:
1. The Speaker decides whether a bill is a Money Bill, and this decision is final and non-justiciable.
2. The Speaker can allow a member of the house to speak in their mother tongue even if they do not know Hindi or English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Speaker's decision on a Money Bill is final and beyond court challenge. The Speaker also maintains order, permits members to address the house in their mother tongue if they cannot adequately express themselves in the official languages of the state/assembly.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly:
1. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly.
2. Such a resolution can be moved without giving any prior notice of at least 14 days to the Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 179(c) stipulates removal by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly. Statement 2 is incorrect: A mandatory prior notice of at least 14 days is required to move such a resolution.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the casting vote of the Speaker:
1. The casting vote can be exercised by the Speaker on any bill or resolution during regular voting.
2. The main purpose of the casting vote is to resolve a deadlock or tie to maintain status quo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Speaker does not vote in the first instance; they only have a casting vote. Statement 2 is correct: The casting vote is used exclusively when there is a tie (equality of votes) to break the deadlock and preserve status quo.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pro-Tem Speaker:
1. The Constitution of India explicitly outlines the detailed appointment process and powers of the Pro-Tem Speaker.
2. The Pro-Tem Speaker ceases to hold office as soon as the new Speaker is elected by the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The term 'Pro-Tem Speaker' is not even mentioned in the Constitution of India; it is an office created by parliamentary conventions and rules. Statement 2 is correct: The Pro-Tem Speaker's office exists only until the House elects its regular Speaker.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the relationship between the Speaker and Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule):
1. The Speaker's decision on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is final and cannot be reviewed by courts under any circumstances.
2. The Supreme Court in Kihoto Hollohan case ruled that the Speaker acts as a tribunal when deciding defection cases and is subject to judicial review.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the original provision making the Speaker's decision final and barred from courts was struck down by the Supreme Court in the Kihoto Hollohan case. Statement 2 is correct: The court held that the Speaker acts as a tribunal and decisions are subject to judicial review on limited grounds.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the emoluments and salary of the Speaker:
1. The salary and allowances of the Speaker are determined by the State Legislature by law.
2. They are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State and are not subject to the annual vote of the legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under Article 186, the salaries and allowances of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are fixed by the State Legislature and charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State under Article 202(3), ensuring financial security and independence.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative role of the Speaker in the Legislative Assembly:
1. The Speaker is the ex-officio chairman of all parliamentary committees of the assembly of which they are a member.
2. The Speaker exercises administrative control over the Secretariat of the Legislative Assembly independently of the executive.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Speaker is the chairman of some specific committees like the Business Advisory Committee and Rules Committee, but not all committees of which they are a member. Statement 2 is correct: The Speaker has supreme administrative control over the Assembly Secretariat, ensuring independence from executive interference.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional position of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly vis-a-vis the Governor:
1. The Speaker communicates all official bills passed by the assembly directly to the President, bypassing the Governor.
2. The Speaker certifies Money Bills and authenticates bills passed by the assembly before they are presented to the Governor for assent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Bills passed by the assembly are presented to the Governor for assent, not directly to the President (except in specific cases where the Governor reserves a bill for the President). Statement 2 is correct: The Speaker certifies Money Bills and authenticates bills passed by the assembly before presentation to the Governor.
